creator: Alexander Terp
description:
27 boilerplate lambdas across 10 scripts exist only to colorize a column, and two idiom generations coexist - 10 in the newer ctx form, 17 in the old global-column form. Ranked fourth by the team-scripts report at high confidence, then dropped from the synthesis; its own critic flagged the omission.

This is the cheapest slice of the table-ergonomics work whose larger design fork sits in stretch. It doesn't depend on that fork landing.

---

### Orientation

- Column modifiers are a grammar-level construct, not a function. Three exist today - `color`, `map`, `filter` - and adding a fourth touches every layer from the grammar down.
- The chain, end to end:
  - Grammar node kinds: `rts/rl/consts.go:88-90` (`rad_field_mod_color`, `rad_field_mod_map`, `rad_field_mod_filter`).
  - CST to AST: `rts/converter.go:1570-1582`.
  - AST node: `rl.RadFieldMod` (`rts/rl/ast_types.go:623-640`) - a container level holding target field names, and individual levels holding `ModType` plus args.
  - Runtime: `radInvocation.applyModifier` (`core/rad_block.go:192-233`), a switch on `mod.ModType`.
  - Render: mods reach go-tbl through `tbl.SetColumnColoring(r.colToMods)` (`core/rad_block.go:362`).
- The existing `color` modifier is *not* what this card wants. `color` takes a literal color plus a regex (`core/rad_block.go:198-215`), stored as `radColorMod{color, regex}` (`core/rad_block.go:245-248`). `colorize` derives a distinct color per distinct value from an enum - that is `FuncColorize` in `core/func_colorize.go`, which sorts the enum and calls `GetEnumColor`. Today the only way to combine them is `map fn(x, ctx) colorize(x, [...])`, which is the boilerplate the card is counting.

### Where to start

Settle the design question before touching anything: **where does the enum come from?**

`ctx.src` - an immutable snapshot of the full column, documented at `docs-web/docs/guide/rad-blocks.md:317-319` - is the obvious answer. A bare `colorize` modifier with no arguments could derive the enum from the column's distinct values, which is precisely what the 27 hand-written lambdas do. An explicit-enum form (`colorize ["a","b","c"]`) may also be wanted for stable colors across runs with different data. Decide both before writing grammar, because the grammar encodes the answer.

Then, in order:

1. **Grammar (upstream).** `go.mod:14` pins `github.com/amterp/tree-sitter-rad v0.6.0`; the checkout is at `~/src/tree-sitter-rad`. Iterate with a local `replace` directive and **remove it before committing** - `./dev --release` refuses to release with one present.
2. `rts/rl/consts.go` - new `K_RAD_FIELD_MOD_COLORIZE`.
3. `rts/converter.go:1570-1582` - new case.
4. `rts/check/` - the checker has to accept the new keyword.
5. `core/rad_block.go:192-233` - new `case "colorize":` in `applyModifier`.
6. Render: `radColorMod` is a `{color, regex}` pair, so a per-value derived color either compiles down to one regex per distinct value, or needs a new mod shape that go-tbl can consume. Check whether `go-tbl` (first-party, `go.mod:10`, checkout at `~/src/go-tbl`) needs a change too.

`rts/radfmt` likely needs nothing - per `rts/radfmt/AGENTS.md`, block constructs including `rad` blocks are still `verbatim()`, so the formatter re-emits their source span. Verify rather than assume, and if a rule does change, `rts/radfmt/RULES.md` must move with it (the golden rule in that guide).

### How to verify

```sh
make generate
make build
./bin/radd table.rad
go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=tables
go test ./rts -run TestSTSnapshots -update=st_snapshots
go test ./rts/check/ -run TestCheckSnapshots
make test
```

The `=` in `-update=...` is required. Syntax-tree snapshots live in `rts/test/st_snapshots/`, table behavior in `core/testing/snapshots/tables/`.

### Done when

- A rad block can colorize a column by distinct value without a lambda, and the output matches what the equivalent `map fn(x, ctx) colorize(...)` produces today.
- Syntax-tree, checker, and table snapshots all cover the new modifier, including it combined with `map` and `filter` on the same column.
- `docs-web/docs/guide/rad-blocks.md` documents it alongside `color` (line 433 onward) and `map`/`filter`. Its snippets are executed by `core/testing/docs_snippets_test.go`, so the example must actually run.
- `make generate` committed; no `replace` directive in `go.mod`.

### Watch out for

This card cannot fully land without a `tree-sitter-rad` release, and tagging first-party libs stays with the maintainer. Say so up front rather than discovering it at commit time.

Colors derived from a column's distinct values are only stable while the data is. If one run's data lacks a value, every color after it in the sorted enum shifts - `core/func_colorize.go` sorts the enum before assigning. That is already true of the lambda idiom, but making it a first-class modifier makes it look more authoritative than it is. Consider whether the explicit-enum form should be the documented default for anything a human compares across runs.
title: Make colorize a first-class column modifier
